items.note: Gemeenteblad 2026-84587 (published 26-02-2026, in force the day after publication). The decision is taken by the college van burgemeester en wethouders (the executive), not by the council: 'Het college ... besluit', 'vastgesteld in de openbare vergadering van 17 februari 2026'. Hours as in the draft: zones A and B Mon-Sat 08:00-22:00 and Sun 12:00-18:00; B*, C, D and D* Mon-Sat 08:00-18:00 plus koopavond(en) 18:00-22:00 (the draft leaves out D*); D/WTC Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00. Annex 1 lists Stationsplein, Fonteinland, Jacob Catsplein, Sixmaplein, Oosterbuurt and 'Parkeerterrein Dirk Zeperweg' as pay-parking places. Wrong body (council) is the only error.
items.corrected_text: By decision of 17 February 2026 the executive (college van burgemeester en wethouders) set the 2026 designation of paid and permit-holder parking, published on 26 February 2026 and in force the day after publication. Tariff zones A and B charge Monday to Saturday 08:00-22:00 and Sunday 12:00-18:00 (public holidays excepted); zones B*, C, D and D* charge Monday to Saturday 08:00-18:00 plus shopping evenings (koopavond) until 22:00; zone D/WTC charges Monday to Friday 08:00-18:00. The list of paid street places includes Stationsplein, Fonteinland, Jacob Catsplein, Sixmaplein, Oosterbuurt and the Dirk Zeperweg car park.

items.note: PDF 'Tarieventabel behorende bij de Verordening parkeerbelastingen Leeuwarden 2026' (footer: 'Behorende bij het raadsbesluit van 5 november 2025'). Per 60 minutes: zone A 3.50 (non-disabled space), B 2.10, B* 2.10, C 1.40, D 0.90, D* 0.90, D/WTC 0.90; zone D day rate 4.60 Mon-Sat. Cross-checked against the adopted ordinance on lokaleregelgeving.overheid.nl (CVDR748301, valid from 2 Dec 2025, levy from 1 Jan 2026, 'vastgesteld ... 5 november 2025'): identical figures. Title and date match.

Same tariff table, read in full. Resident permit 286 per calendar year in zones 1-4, 143 in zones 6-10, 36.60 for Grou; business permit 570 (zones 1-4) and 286 (zones 6-10); day permit 16.60 (zones 1-4) and 4.70 (zones 6-10); day exemption 29.00 for streets with an entry ban or restriction (Nieuwestad, Peperstraat, Wirdumerdijk, Sint Jacobstraat). All as in the draft and also in the adopted ordinance CVDR748301.

PDF 'Tarievenbesluit parkeergarages Leeuwarden 2023', header 'Geldend voor 2023-2025', 'Alleen de tarieven exclusief BTW', adopted 9 Nov 2022, effective 1 Jan 2023 (art. 8.3). Zaailand and Oldehoofsterkerkhof 1.65 per 60 min, 8.26 max per day (above 300 min), evening 19:00-06:00 max 3.31. Klanderij and De Revius 1.40/h, day max 5.79; Hoeksterend 1.40/h, max 3.31 (above 140 min). Zaailand resident annual pass (bewoners binnenstad) 636.36. The text dates these correctly as 2023 figures excluding VAT and says no 2026 decision was found; a May 2025 council proposal (2025-108206, read for item 14) mentions an intended average 10% garage tariff rise per 2026, so figures are old.

CVDR435579 'Tarievenbesluit parkeergarages Leeuwarden 2017' (valid 21-12-2016 to 09-03-2018, adopted 7 Nov 2016, effective 1 Jan 2017). Zaailand and Oldehoofsterkerkhof 2.07 per 60 min (excl. VAT), max per day 7.27 (above 480 min). Garages listed include Klanderij, Tesselschadestraat, Hoeksterend, Zaailand, Oldehoofsterkerkhof and Oosterstraat. Comparison with the 2023 decision (1.65/h, 8.26 day max) is arithmetically right. Historic, expired regulation, and the item says so.

Parkeerbeleidsplan 2015 (PDF created 22 June 2015), section 2.1.1: 'ruim 5.200 parkeerplaatsen', bijna 1800 paid on-street, bijna 500 permit-holder on-street, ruim 2500 in five garages, ruim 250 at the P+R site, bijna 250 at the Leeuwarder Courant site; capacity 'in de gemiddelde situatie ruim voldoende'; occupancy falls after 2011 except Saturdays. One overstatement: the plan says local shortages are felt 'vooral' for short shop visits, 'bijvoorbeeld' at Eewal and Tweebaksmarkt, i.e. examples, not the only places. Counts date from about 2014 and should be labelled old.
items.corrected_text: The 2015 parking policy plan (using counts up to about 2014) put the number of parking spaces in the city centre at just over 5,200: nearly 1,800 paid street spaces, nearly 500 permit-holder street spaces and over 2,500 spaces in five garages, plus about 250 at the P+R site and nearly 250 at the Leeuwarder Courant site. It judged capacity on average more than sufficient, with occupancy falling after 2011 except on Saturdays, but noted local shortages for short shop visits, for example at Eewal and Tweebaksmarkt. These figures are about a decade old.

items.note: Same 2015 plan. Garages Zaailand, Oldehove, Klanderij, Hoeksterend and Oosterstraat are 'de primaire parkeerlocaties voor bezoekers van het centrum'; 'kosten voor parkeren worden in essentie door de gebruiker betaald'; policy 'restrictief waar sprake is van schaarste ..., het openbaar gebied minder op auto's is ingericht en waar alternatieven beschikbaar zijn' (the draft compresses the three conditions); 'in alle parkeergarages kentekenherkenning ingevoerd en kan met alle betaalwijzen worden betaald'; 'Het schilgebied rond het centrum is gereguleerd met een blauwe zone' with the aim of keeping out long-stay parking. Historic, 2015, as the item says.

PDF 'Wijziging vennootschapscontract' (notary file PJD\2019.001393.01) is an unsigned draft: date left as '@', council/college decision 'van @ tweeduizend twintig', notary deed placeholders. Recitals: C.V. (set up 19 June 2000, amended 2009) runs De Klanderij, Oldehove, Hoeksterend (Bastion) and Wilhelminaplein (Zaailand); the municipality is 'commanditaire vennoot' and Parkeergarages Leeuwarden B.V. (Zaailand 5) 'beherend vennoot'. The draft's wording matches the page and flags that the deed is unsigned. Keep confidence low: a draft is not proof of the final structure. The 2015 plan and the 2025 bicycle-garage proposal instead name the Stichting Parkeergarages as operator, so the summary should not state the partnership structure as fact.

Antwoord B&W op schriftelijke vragen (Lijst058, filed 4 April 2024), zaaknummer 2024-079440, dated Leeuwarden 7 May 2024. Answer 1: limited grid capacity (expansion in garages currently not possible except Hoeksterend) and fire-brigade requirements for underground garages; 3b: expansion in Oldehove or Zaailand is 'ongewenst', so above-ground Hoeksterend and Klanderij chosen. 2a: garage charging rate EUR 0.70 incl. VAT, set yearly by the board of Stichting Parkeergarages, 'in mei worden de tarieven opnieuw bepaald'. The questioners say Zaailand has only two charging points. The 0.70 figure is the April 2024 rate and may since have changed.

parking.net copy of IP Parking press release, 'Monday, September 30, 2024': 'installation of 76 new charging stations' in Hoeksterend, 'prepared for an expansion up to 352 charging points' via load balancing software, free charging 25 to 30 September. It is a supplier press release (the item says so); the council answer of May 2024 (item 8) independently speaks of a rise from 2 to 76 with possible extension to about 350, so medium confidence is fair. The press release uses 'charging stations' for the 76 and 'charging points' for 352.

Brief aan de gemeenteraad 'Verkenning zero-emissie-zone Leeuwarden', 2024-077762, dated 23 April 2024. Consultant RHDHV (2023): ZE zone for freight traffic and delivery vans (not passenger cars) is 'haalbaar en wenselijk', best size is the area inside the parking ring, introduction on 1 January 2028 'realistisch'. Next steps: consultation of local businesses in Q2 2024; announcement decision 'naar verwachting later in 2024'; final traffic decision about a year before introduction. Worded as a proposal, status unknown, as required. In the summary, say the date was the consultant's view, not a decision.

CVDR747805 Parkeerverordening Leeuwarden 2025: 'gelezen het voorstel van het college van 14 oktober 2025'; adopted 'in de openbare vergadering van 12 november 2025'; the version read (version 2) is 'Geldend van 19-06-2026 t/m heden'. Art. 8-17 provide resident, visitor, business, care-provider, commercial car-sharing, day and blue-zone permits (all 'kan', the college may grant). Art. 18: college may set a permit ceiling per zone; applicants go on a waiting list for undetermined time. Art. 19(1): application refused for city-centre addresses (zones 1 and 2 fully, 3 and 4 partly) where an exemption from the parking requirement was granted. Date 2026-06-19 is the start of this consolidated version; the council adopted the regulation on 12 Nov 2025 (worth stating).

Motie 'betaald parkeren blauwe zones, eerst een pilot', council meeting 16 October 2024, on the Beleidskader Mobiliteit 2040, signed by FNP and VVD members. It states 'in het beleidskader mobiliteit staat dat in alle blauwe zones betaald parkeren zal worden ingevoerd' and asks the college to pilot first in zones with most nuisance, evaluate, and only then bring a proposal to the council. The page is only the motion text with no vote result, as the item says. The statement about the framework is the motion's characterisation, not read in the framework itself.

Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 374807, 12 August 2026: Verkeersbesluit VB-26-42, decision date 30 July 2026, by the college, to designate two parking places with E8 signs and subsign 'Commshare' as car-share locations at parking lot Trefplak, Redbadwei. Considerations: two places with charging posts are used for the two electric shared vehicles; pilot with Commshare in the Middelsee district; shared cars reduce car ownership and parking pressure (general rationale, CROW). The pilot's stated aim is to stimulate shared mobility; the car-ownership aim is the general reasoning for shared cars.

Raadsvoorstel 'Krediet realisatie en exploitatie fietsenstalling Nieuwestad', 2025-108206, dated 13 May 2025. Former V&D building, ca. 800-1300 bicycles on 1400 m2, total realisation cost EUR 1,960,000 excl. VAT, funded 1,000,000 from a fund, 710,000 from the parking reserve (leaving ca. 400,000) and 250,000 from Stichting Parkeergarages; the Stichting will manage it as it does 'de andere twee stallingen'; opening planned mid-2026 (1 July) / Q2 2026; the garage is a precondition for the Nieuwestad redesign. The proposal still needed council approval; the outcome was not read, as the item says. Date can be refined to 2025-05-13.

corrected_summary: Leeuwarden regulates its centre with tariff zones A to D. Under the council's 2026 tariff table (adopted 5 November 2025, levy from 1 January 2026), on-street parking costs 3.50 euros per hour in zone A, 2.10 in zones B and B*, 1.40 in zone C and 0.90 in zones D, D* and D/WTC, with a day rate of 4.60 euros in zone D. According to the executive's designation of 17 February 2026, zones A and B charge Monday to Saturday 08:00-22:00 and Sunday 12:00-18:00, other zones charge until 18:00 with late opening evenings until 22:00, and D/WTC charges Monday to Friday. Resident permits cost 286 euros per year in zones 1-4 and 143 euros in zones 6-10; the parking ordinance, adopted 12 November 2025, lets the college set permit ceilings with waiting lists and refuses permits to city-centre addresses that were granted an exemption from the parking requirement. The central garages (Zaailand, Oldehove, Klanderij, Hoeksterend, De Revius, Oosterstraat) have council-set tariffs excluding VAT; the latest decision read is for 2023-2025 (Zaailand 1.65 euros per hour, day maximum 8.26 euros), so these figures are old, and no 2026 garage decision was found. The garages are run by the Stichting Parkeergarages according to a 2015 plan and a 2025 council proposal, which also names the foundation as manager of the city's guarded bicycle garages; an unsigned 2019 draft deed also describes a partnership between the municipality and Parkeergarages Leeuwarden B.V., but the final structure is unconfirmed. The 2015 parking plan (counts to about 2014) found just over 5,200 city-centre spaces, judged capacity more than sufficient and made garages the primary visitor parking. In an answer of May 2024 the executive said grid capacity and fire-safety rules make extra charging points in the underground garages Oldehove and Zaailand undesirable, so expansion goes to Hoeksterend and Klanderij; a supplier press release of September 2024 reports 76 charging points at Hoeksterend, prepared for up to 352. Proposals and explorations not yet decided include a zero-emission zone for delivery vehicles (a consultant considered 1 January 2028 realistic, reported to the council in April 2024, status unknown), a motion of October 2024 asking for a pilot before paid parking in all blue zones (outcome unknown), and a May 2025 proposal for a guarded bicycle garage on Nieuwestad (council outcome not read). A July 2026 traffic decision reserved two charging spaces at the Trefplak car park in Middelsee for Commshare electric car sharing. The municipal website leeuwarden.nl was still offline (503) when retried, so the low-traffic city centre and park-and-ride could not be checked.
